content.title: Cozy Pic Of Rory McIlroy & Reporter Amanda Balionis Won't Help The Affair Rumors
content.text: Hector Vivas/Getty Images Once the 2026 Masters got in full swing, it seemed there was more to golf than meets the eye, as messy rumors about an affair between Rory McIlroy and reporter Amanda Balionis continued to fly. McIlroy likely knew that he was going to be under intense scrutiny during the tournament as the public kept a close watch for not only his excellent form but also some flirty behavior. Rumors about the golfer and the reporter began in 2024, conveniently right around the time when McIlroy filed for a divorce from Erica Stoll. The Daily Mail was the first to report on this after the two engaged in a flirty interview in which Balionis wasn't wearing her wedding ring. Shortly after, news of McIlroy's divorce filing broke. Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire This photo from 2025 shows the two cozied up together during an interview in Pebble Beach, California, at the Pebble Beach Golf Links. McIlroy has his arm around Balionis in a way that screams more than friends. If anything, McIlroy should have started treading lightly around Balionis, especially considering that he's still married to Stoll. While McIlroy filed for divorce in 2024, the two called it off about a month later, with McIlroy saying in a statement to The Guardian, "Erica and I have realized that our best future was as a family together." The backtrack on the divorce was certainly an interesting choice given the publicity of it all, but the two are still together as of this writing. Rory McIlroy's messy pattern of behavior hasn't helped the affair rumors David Cannon/Getty Images According to Alan Shipnuck's book, "Rory: The Heartache and Triumph of Golf's Most Human Superstar," Rory McIlroy's affair rumors don't come as a surprise. While Shipnuck reports that insiders close to McIlroy and Amanda Balionis maintain that the two were never engaged in an affair, it's a rumor that the public just can't overlook. Shipnuck writes, "That there were rumors about McIlroy's love life wasn't totally surprising given his ribald streak." Apparently, McIlroy is prone to reckless behavior, and has even been compared to the notorious Tiger Woods. McIlroy has yet to achieve Woods' level of self-destruction, but he's been known to go on mysterious guy trips to Ibiza, which in many ways is temptation island for a man with a fragile marriage. McIlroy's wife, Erica Stoll, is often compared to Woods' ex-wife, Elin Nordegren. The two's similarities stem from their desire to remain private, never providing interviews or insight into their lives as the wives of athletes at the top of their game. Despite their differing personalities, McIlroy reportedly still chose to court Stoll back in 2012, when he was still dating tennis star Caroline Wozniacki. There's no proof that any infidelity occurred while the athletes were dating, but McIlroy's reckless behavior made itself apparent as their relationship developed. McIlroy started dating Stoll a few months after breaking off his engagement with Wozniacki. Given McIlroy's pattern of behavior, rumors of an affair with Balionis don't seem like anything out of the ordinary. Celebrities Who Treat Their Significant Others Like Trash Getty Images Love isn't easy, but it's a whole lot harder when your significant other treats you like utter trash. Though Hollywood relationships are notoriously short-lived (blame the pressures of fame and red carpet-worthy egos,) some stars are undeniably terrible partners. From Gwyneth Paltrow, who's totally willing to admit she's hard to date, to Chris Brown, who was put on probation for his disturbing crimes against Rihanna, the spectrum of inconsiderate partners is notably vast. There are hundreds of ways to hurt the one you love — and even more if you've got money. Not every celebrity bad boy (or girl) stays that way, though. Some regretful partners actually do change. Take Adam Levine, for example, who allegedly apologized to his exes before settling down, or Justin Bieber, whose plea for forgiveness infected airwaves in 2015. Then there's John Mayer, who still seems sort of bitter about that one Taylor Swift song (yeah, we're still waiting on the world to change, too.) If the bad press is true, these celebrities are notoriously inconsiderate partners whom you wouldn't want to date. Johnny Depp's reputation came under fire C Flanigan/Getty Images Johnny Depp and Amber Heard met while filming 2009's "The Rum Diary," and a volatile romance ensued. The pair married in February 2015, but by the end of May 2016, Heard had filed for divorce. The split came just days after she claimed Depp had been physically abusive on multiple occasions. TMZ obtained an image that appeared to show red bruising on Heard's face, particularly around her eye, which she alleged was the result of her estranged husband hitting her with his iPhone. Heard was eventually granted a restraining order, but Depp denied the allegations. An LAPD spokesman later told People that following their investigation, there was "no evidence of any crime." The contentious he said, she said was the first in a slew of headline-making court cases between the exes. Most notably, Heard wrote an op-ed for The Washington Post in 2018, claiming, "I spoke up against sexual violence — and faced our culture's wrath." She didn't mention Depp by name, but even so, he filed a defamation suit against her in 2019. Along the course of the trial, Depp seemed to not take it very seriously. While Heard made allegations that her ex physically and sexually assaulted her, the actor denied her claims and kept busy doodling and drawing viral sketches with colored markers. He eventually won the lawsuit in 2022 and was awarded $10.4 million in damages. Chris Brown called himself a 'monster' Getty Images In 2008, it seemed like Chris Brown and Rihanna were hip hop's It couple. The pair met as teenagers at the Vibe Awards, and over the next few years, they grew from collaborators to best friends to totally in love. Unfortunately, not all was as rosy as it seemed from the red carpet. In 2009, TMZ released disturbing photographs of Rihanna, who was reportedly beaten by Brown after a pre-Grammy party. Not long after this, the full police report surfaced online, and Brown pleaded guilty to felony assault. He was sentenced to five years probation and six months community labor, reported Billboard. Brown later admitted in the documentary "Chris Brown: Welcome to My Life" (via People) that he "felt like a f***ing monster" after the incident with Rihanna. He eventually did find love with model Karrueche Tran. Unfortunately, old patterns appeared to resurface. According to E! News, Tran alleged Brown punched her in the stomach, pushed her down the stairs, and threatened to shoot and kill her on numerous occasions. Tran was granted a permanent restraining order after sharing angry texts in which Brown threatened to "beat the s***" out of her. Mariah Carey has allegedly 'had issues' Getty Images Mariah Carey has certainly been through the ringer when it comes to love. Her early marriage to her label boss Tommy Mottola was allegedly so abusive that she had to get permission to leave the house. She also endured a traumatic child abuse investigation (she and then-husband Nick Cannon came out in the clear) and a highly publicized mental breakdown. Through it all, Cannon seemed to be a solid support for the troubled singer. It was only after the pair divorced that Carey allegedly started treating her romantic partners like garbage, and it was fiancé James Packer who supposedly bore the brunt of that bad juju. According to Daily Mail, Carey allegedly threw Packer's laptop out a window in 2016 because he played a Beyoncé song. The pair split before tying the knot, with Carey's team claiming she wasn't happy with his behavior. Packer's rep fired back, telling People, "[T]ypical Mariah to just twist things that don't sound good to her. They split because she has issues." The following year, one of Carey's former security guards threatened to sue the songstress for sexual harassment. According to TMZ, he claimed she exposed herself to him and intentionally performed sexual acts while he was in view. Carey came clean about her struggle with bipolar disorder in early 2018, so perhaps she has changed for the better after seeking treatment. Brad Pitt was 'boozing or had a spliff' every day Getty Images Brad Pitt has certainly had some tumultuous relationships, and if you asked his ex-wives, he seems to be the common denominator. In the early '00s, Pitt's divorce from Jennifer Aniston prompted the press to essentially frame the actress as the world's saddest lady for the rest of her career. What happened? Pitt supposedly had an emotional affair with co-star Angelina Jolie on the set of "Mr. and Mrs. Smith." The new lovers claimed they took things to the next level only after his split with Aniston, though Pitt later said the aforementioned movie is his favorite because, as he told Rolling Stone, it's where he "fell in love." And get this: Before Pitt's divorce from Aniston was finalized, he posed for an epic W magazine photo shoot with Jolie. The piece, titled "Domestic Bliss," cast the two "friends" as a sexy husband and wife with kids. In response, Aniston told Vanity Fair that Pitt has "a sensitivity chip that's missing." As for Brangelina, they appeared to have it good for nearly a decade, but in 2016, they went through an explosive breakup and nasty custody battle. Pitt told GQ that substance abuse was at the root of his relationship's "self-inflicted" collapse. "I can't remember a day since I got out of college when I wasn't boozing or had a spliff, or something," he said. Though that all sounds awful trashy, Pitt has since reportedly embarked on a cleaner lifestyle. Calvin Harris: perhaps not the best romantic collaborator Getty Images It seems like mixing business with pleasure is a recipe for disaster — at least for Calvin Harris' girlfriends. The Scottish DJ has a terrible track record when it comes to working with his significant others. His 2014 split with pop star Rita Ora seemed amicable until Harris allegedly blindsided her by publicly announcing their breakup on Twitter (via Billboard) months after the fact — weird, but okay. Things got worse from there. Ora was scheduled to perform her hit "I Will Never Let You Down" at the 2014 Teen Choice Awards, but Harris reportedly wouldn't give her legal permission to do so. Ora had to cancel the performance because Harris owned the copyright. If Harris' experience with Ora didn't reach peak-level petty, the demise of his relationship with Taylor Swift certainly did. The drama unfolded when fans discovered Swift helped write Harris' Rihanna collaboration, "This Is What You Came For." Swift used the pseudonym "Nils Sjoberg" to reportedly avoid overshadowing anyone on the track (girl gets a lot of attention). After its release, Harris claimed he "couldn't see" himself working with Swift — something Swift's camp apparently took as a mega-burn and whad'ya know, word soon got out that Swift helped Harris write the track. Harris eventually came clean, but in the same breath, he also accused his ex of trying to make him look bad in a Twitter tantrum (via Us Weekly). As ill-fated as that tweetstorm was, Harris did eventually apologize. Justin Bieber's sorry track record Getty Images Back in 2018, Jalena was still an inescapable force. The notorious relationship began in 2010 when Selena Gomez and Justin Bieber were innocent teens on an innocent date at IHOP. Oh, how things went so wrong in a few long years (it felt like a lifetime, did it not?). Bieber was reportedly not the best boyfriend to sweet Gomez. After all, he allegedly penned the track "Sorry" about the "Good for You" songstress. What does he have to be sorry for? A whole lot. Some highlights include the time he got into a fist fight with Orlando Bloom after allegedly hooking up with Bloom's ex-wife. This move seemed purely spiteful because Gomez was rumored to be canoodling with Bloom at the time. While Gomez was struggling with Lupus, Biebs was busy getting arrested for drunk driving and resisting arrest, egging his neighbor's home, and urinating in a custodian's mop bucket. Classy. Though they had both dated other people when apart, these two kept winding up together. In 2018, after reportedly reuniting for the umpteenth time, Gomez's mom, Mandy Teefey, admitted in an interview with Gossip Cop that she was "not happy" about the rumored return of the Biebs (via Teen Vogue). Adam Levine owed a lot of ladies apologies Getty Images Adam Levine may have a voice that's sweet as sugar, but the way he's acted in past relationships is anything but. Lavine allegedly dumped his supermodel girlfriend Nina Agdal by completely ghosting her. According to Us Weekly, he stopped answering her calls, then eventually informed her of his engagement to on-and-off flame and fellow model Behati Prinsloo through a text message. Levine certainly has a way with words in his songs, but when it comes to real-life communication, that's apparently not the case. He allegedly also dumped Jessica Simpson via text message. He embarrassed cocktail waitress Rebecca Ginos by telling Howard Stern (via E! News) they had sex on the first day they met, and he shamed actress Lindsay Lohan by simultaneously saying that he never slept with her and that she probably slept with a lot of people. Oh, and he reportedly mortified Victoria's Secret model Anne Vyalitsyna by telling the world they used the "pull-out method" (via The Daily Beast). It seems Levine has never been one for relationship tact, though he did allegedly reach out to his exes to apologize before marrying Prinsloo in the summer of 2014. Tom Cruise: relationship impossible Getty Images Most of us remember Tom Cruise's relationships by their fairy-tale moments, like his famous movies alongside Nicole Kidman, or that time he jumped on Oprah's couch to exuberantly proclaim his love for Katie Holmes. What we don't remember are how those love stories played out. Amid his growing dedication to Scientology in 2001, Cruise abruptly filed for divorce from Kidman after 10 years of marriage. Though Kidman admitted to DuJour Magazine (via People) that it was a "shock to [her] system," she did quip to David Letterman (via The Standard), "At least I can wear heels now." In no world is stealthily exiting a decade-long marriage like it's "Mission: Impossible" commendable behavior, but apparently, Cruise did it anyway. His relationship with Katie Holmes, which was long rumored to be a contract marriage, may have been even more out of control. According to Mirror, Holmes had to follow a long list of bizarre marriage rules, including complete silence during labor. She allegedly wasn't allowed to utter a single peep while delivering Suri, and according to some reports, she feared for her safety after filing for divorce because of the church. Of course, this is speculation at its finest, but it's certainly the kind of trash talking that would make us wary of another Cruise wedding. Gwyneth Paltrow: architect of misery? Getty Images Gwyneth Paltrow has painted herself a well-intentioned (albeit sometimes clueless) wealthy single mama. She spends her days promoting bizarre vaginal steam spas and $1,220 casserole dishes. Nothing about her carefully crafted image would lead us to believe she's a terrible romantic partner, but the actress has admitted she has her flaws. "I'm actually a pretty good friend, and a good sister and daughter and mother, but I'm at my potentially most vulnerable and f***ed up in the romantic slice of the pie," she told "Girlboss Radio" (via E! News). Paltrow does at least make an effort to "consciously uncouple" rather than ghosting her flames, and that's probably why she remains in good standing with most of her exes. However, that doesn't mean dating the Oscar-winning actress is all roses. According to E! News, cheating rumors emerged when Paltrow was spotted kissing her ex, Donovan Leitch, at a Dodgers game just six days after announcing her split from Coldplay frontman Chris Martin. In the past, Paltrow has admitted that her relationships rarely make it past six weeks and that — as she told Diane Sawyer (via ABC News) — she's sometimes the "architect of [her] own misery." Well, at least she's honest. Rob Kardashian takes social media rants to a whole new level Getty Images Kardashians generally take the moral high road when it comes to relationships — from Khloé Kardashian supporting her troubled ex-husband during his recovery to Kris Jenner supporting her ex-husband's transition into womanhood long after their divorce. Rob Kardashian is the exception to the rule. Rob's relationship with Blac Chyna seemed insanely tumultuous by tabloid accounts. These included the explosive fights documented throughout their reality TV show, "Rob & Chyna," abuse claims and restraining orders, and their apparent affinity for airing their grievances on social media. In 2017, after an exhausting year and a half of on-and-off dating, Chyna took to Snapchat (via Us Weekly) to claim Rob beat her up. She also allegedly sent Rob a video of herself kissing another man in an effort to get him to leave her alone. Rob countered by posting several explicit photos of her online in what appeared to be some sort of deranged (and potentially criminal) hours-long social media rant. This incident was the final straw for Chyna, who filed a restraining order. Her lawyer, Lisa Bloom, had this to say in a statement (via CNN): "Mr. Kardashian, you are now on notice: revenge porn is illegal. Cyberbullying your ex is harassment. ... Your attempts to shame and control [Chyna] are hereby rejected." Emma Roberts: love story or horror story? Getty Images Actress Emma Roberts may look like an innocent girl next door, but that doesn't mean she isn't vicious when it comes to matters of the heart. Rumor has it the actress physically abused her boyfriend, actor Evan Peters. The couple reportedly met while filming "Adult World" and were later cast together in "American Horror Story." For the first year or so of their relationship, they were the poster children for millennial power couples. Then came 2013, when Roberts was arrested for allegedly assaulting Peters in Canada, as TMZ reported. Though Peters reportedly suffered a bloody nose and bite marks, he didn't press charges, and Roberts was released. According to a totally real and not at all made up source that spoke to OK! magazine, Roberts has also brought her problematic relationship issues to set. "Basically, as soon as the director yells, 'Cut,' Emma and Evan are making out. That is, if they're not screaming at each other," said the anonymous insider. The two later got engaged but called it quits in 2019, putting their trashy moments together behind them for good. Ronnie Ortiz-Magro, maybe lay off the Ron Ron Juice? Getty Images You don't have to watch "Jersey Shore" for long to realize Ronnie Ortiz-Magro doesn't have much tact when it comes to relationships. Audiences may recall the anonymous note some housemates typed to warn Sammi "Sweetheart" Giancola about her man's trifling ways. The infamous note (via MTV) said that when Giancola wasn't around, Ortiz-Magro "put his head between a cocktail waitress' breasts," made out with two girls, and "was grinding with multiple fat women." Believe it or not: Those weren't his worst offenses. As Life & Style reported, the star's relationship with Giancola was the most toxic on the show. How could it not be when it was clouded with a heavy stream of "Ron Ron Juice" and fights that escalated to the point where he actually tried to throw Giancola and her entire bed onto the porch? If you think Giancola had it bad, you haven't yet seen "Jersey Shore: Family Vacation." After Ortiz-Magro settled into the Miami house, it didn't take long for him to completely forget about his pregnant girlfriend Jen Harley. He invited a group of girls back to use the hot tub and did something suspicious behind a closed bathroom door. Later that year, Ortiz-Magro appeared to have a physical fight with Harley on Instagram Live. We should mention that Harley was arrested for domestic battery after allegedly dragging her baby's daddy with a car, as Us Weekly reported, so let's give thanks these two have since called it quits. Jax Taylor can't pump the breaks on his wandering eye Getty Images Every reality show needs a villain. For "Vanderpump Rules," Jax Taylor is the guy for the job. Sure, Taylor has done some pretty noble things in his time on the Bravo series. He paid for girlfriend Brittany Cartwright's breast implants and even convinced her to go bigger than planned. "I'm ready to throw some Ds on this," he told doctors (via Daily Mail). "Go big or go home." What a sweetheart, right? Wrong. Fans who've been with the series since the start remember when the reality stud cheated on Stassi Schroeder with her best friend, Kristen Doute. Years later, Schroeder introduced him on her podcast "Straight Up With Stassi" (via Bravo) as a guy who did "bad things on the reg." Taylor has been surprisingly open about his flaws (at least the ones he's self-aware enough to recognize). He admitted to Schroeder that he "didn't think" before cheating. "I just did it, and I didn't care." Cartwright and Taylor became an item after meeting in Vegas in 2015. Though she claimed to Bravo's The Daily Dish that he fell in love with her "at first sight," he's got a funny way of showing it. According to Bustle, he floated a salacious rumor that he walked in on Cartwright having sex with Doute, but in reality, he was the one sneaking around. In Season 6, we learned that Taylor slept with ex-SURver Faith Stowers and had been trashing Cartwright, as Us Weekly reported. He has since sought reiki healing. We've lost count of Jesse James' affairs Getty Images There's a reason Jesse James is a notorious Hollywood bad boy. The guy has a terrible track record with women. Beloved Oscar-winning actress Sandra Bullock famously divorced the "Monster Garage" star after he was caught cheating on her with the kind of gal who'd allegedly tattoo a swastika on her stomach. Not only did he mess with Miss Congeniality, but he also told Daily Mail that cheating is a "part of life" and "a lot of good" came from the dissolution of his marriage. Nice, right? Mistreating America's sweetheart wasn't an isolated incident. According to People, he announced his engagement to tattoo artist Kat Von D less than a year after divorcing Bullock, telling Howard Stern (via Us Weekly) that she was better in bed. Six months later, Von D called off the wedding, claiming in a lengthy Facebook post that James cheated on her with 19 different women. Shocking, right? James them moved on to wife No. 4, billionaire heiress Alexis DeJoria, who had been subject to the same cheating scandals as the women before her. In an interview with InTouch, hair stylist Myla Harris claimed she exchanged racy social media messages with James during his relationship with DeJoria. Was this — or the fact that by 2020, DeJoria and James had decided to divorce — really news? Kristen Stewart sucked the life out of her Twilight lover Getty Images Kristen Stewart may not have treated all her partners like trash, but she certainly did a doozy on Robert Pattinson. The "Twilight" lovers had the kind of glittering romance that Hollywood dies for (figuratively, of course, considering vampires live forever). Less than four months before the premiere of "Twilight's" final installment, Stewart found herself embroiled in one of young Hollywood's most shocking cheating scandals. According to Us Weekly, she became romantically involved with director Rupert Sanders while filming "Snow White and the Huntsman." When photos emerged of the pair making out, "Twilight" fans were stunned. Sanders had a wife and children, by the way. "I lit my universe on fire and I watched it burn," the actress told Marie Claire (via Daily Mail) at the time. "Speaking very candidly, it was a really traumatic period in my early 20s that kick-started something in me that was a bit more feral." So there you have it. She's more werewolf than vampire, after all. Sienna Miller may have been a Bond villain in training Getty Images When you catch your British hunk cheating with the nanny, it's time to get yourself a James Bond-worthy love triangle — at least if you're going by the Sienna Miller playbook. According to Reuters, when a tabloid journalist pulled a 007 and hacked into actor Daniel Craig's cellphone, the spy found an incriminating voicemail of Miller saying "I love you" to the James Bond star. She was still with the philandering Jude Law at the time. During the News Corp. phone hacking trial, Miller addressed the incident to London's Old Bailey Court (via Reuters), reportedly describing Craig as her best friend. "Whether or not I was in a relationship with Daniel Craig at the time, it was a very brief encounter," she said. Law also owned up to grilling Craig about the alleged affair during the trial. The starlet has admitted to doing "immoral" things. "When I wasn't at work, I wasn't behaving the way you should," she told Esquire (via Us Weekly). Perhaps she was referring to the whatever-it-was with Craig, or maybe she was alluding to her affair with actor Balthazar Getty, who was married with four children when he ran off with Miller. "I probably seem like not a particularly nice person, not a girl's girl," she told GQ (via Us Weekly). Peter Cook reportedly likes them young Getty Images Model Christie Brinkley and architect Peter Cook had a notoriously nasty divorce battle. In an interview with Matt Lauer (via Us Weekly), Brinkley claimed her husband was purposely making her miserable. "I just want peace. And every time I have any joy or any kind of success in anything, he has to try to destroy it," she said. Here's the thing: Peter Cook didn't just cheat on Brinkley — he reportedly cheated on her with a teenager he hired as an assistant. According to "Today" (via People) Cook met Diana Bianchi when she was 18 years old. Their trysts occurred at the office and in Brinkley's homes in The Hamptons. During their divorce trial (via The Sydney Morning Herald), Bianchi testified that Cook "hid cash for her under a rock and gave her $15,000 to help her buy a Nissan Maxima." When the affair ended, he reportedly sent Bianchi a $300,000 payout because he was concerned about her filing a sexual harassment lawsuit. According to Page Six, Cook's divorce from Suzanne Shaw was equally ugly. She claimed in an email that he had a "pathological" desire for young women and filmed himself with a prostitute. Page Six also reported that he was spotted taking "creepy" photos of girls without their knowledge and snuggling up to a 21-year-old student. Eminem was a 'bad husband' Getty Images Eminem may be a rap icon, but the star rose to fame off the back of controversial lyrics that depicted extreme violence against women. Some of his songs targeted his ex-wife Kim Mathers, the mother of his child. A track titled "Kim" depicts a disturbing fantasy about a murder-suicide. It was so vulgar it was left off the clean version of "The Marshall Mathers LP." In an interview with Dr. Keith Ablow (via People), Kim claimed Eminem's abuse led her to attempt suicide. Things reportedly came to a head when she saw her on-and-off husband beating up a blow-up doll that looked like her onstage. "When Marshall's first tour started is when his ego just went 'poof,'" she told Ablow. "Like he was God, that's what he thought. ... I was just told that I should be grateful that he still talks to me." In 2017, Eminem released the track "Bad Husband," in which he apologizes to his ex-wife. Wilmer Valderrama kissed and told and told and told Getty Images Wilmer Valderrama — yes, the dude who played Fez on "That '70s Show" — is one of Hollywood's most covert playboys. His dating history reads like a who's who of early '00s teen stars. Though Us Weekly reported that the actor remained a rock for long-term girlfriend Demi Lovato after their relationship ended, he wasn't always such a loyal guy. The actor revealed some not-so-nice things during a salacious interview with Howard Stern. According to The Daily Beast, he gave actress Jennifer Love Hewitt a sex rating of eight; called singer Ashlee Simpson "a screamer," and commented on actress Lindsay Lohan's waxing habits. The class act also allegedly lied about taking Mandy Moore's virginity, claiming, "The sex with Mandy was good, but it wasn't like warm apple pie." Moore told Elle that Valderrama's story was "utterly tacky," untrue, and hurtful. If you date this guy, you may want to make him sign a nondisclosure agreement. Kris Jenner's cheating is her 'biggest regret' Getty Images Kris Jenner is running an empire, but somehow, she still had time for the odd affair. There have long been rumors that the Kardashian matriarch bedded O.J. Simpson — and that the football star is Khloé Kardashian's real father. Those rumors, which Simpson refuted, are so notorious that Khloé even cracked a joke about them in 2016. The truth is that Kris did have an affair but not with Simpson (at least as far as we know). According to Us Weekly, the momager owned up to cheating on Simpson's attorney, Robert Kardashian, with soccer player-turned-animator Todd Waterman in her 2011 memoir "Kris Jenner ... And All Things Kardashian." On an episode of "Kocktails With Khloé," the "Revenge Body" star admitted that her mother's cheating "destroyed" her father and remains one of Kris' biggest regrets. "I had the happiest life you could've dreamt about," Kris said during an interview on "OBJECTified" (via Us Weekly). "But when you're in something, sometimes people think the grass is always greener, and that was, like, what I think I went through at some point." According to Daily Mail, Waterman admitted Kris was still sleeping with him when she started dating Caitlyn Jenner, meaning she may have cheated on two different people with the same guy. John Mayer roasted his exes Getty Images It's no secret that John Mayer has a reputation as a womanizer. Whether it's totally warranted or not is up for debate. The singer claimed to The New York Times in 2017 that he hadn't dated a lot of people "in the last five, six years." Unfortunately, his good behavior didn't erase his extensive Hollywood dating history, which is peppered with some not-so-nice moments. The singer-songwriter famously humiliated Jessica Simpson, calling her "sexual napalm" in a Playboy interview (via Us Weekly). In the same interview, he referred to his, um, little John (yup, his penis) as a "white supremacist" because he had never been with a person of color. Despite those poorly thought-out comments, Mayer somehow found himself in the arms of Taylor Swift. His 2009 relationship with the then-19-year-old was short-lived, but her alleged breakup song will live on forever. Swift penned a scathing track titled "Dear John," and rumors swirled that Mayer was her muse. He told Rolling Stone at the time that he thought it was "cheap songwriting" and said he felt "humiliated." Swift claimed to Glamour that this was "presumptuous" because she never technically said it was about him. We don't know who occupies the moral high ground on this one, but one thing is clear: Mayer still wouldn't let it go. In 2016, he tweeted (via NME) that Swift's birthday is the "lamest day of the year." He was 39 years old at the time. And speaking of Swift... Taylor Swift has had a big reputation Getty Images Taylor Swift might be a peach when she's in a relationship, but her exes often sing a totally different tune. The "Reputation" songstress has a notorious rep for doling out biting remarks and trashing her exes in her hit songs. According to People, Swift made a big deal about Joe Jonas allegedly dumping her in a 27-second phone call, but the Jonas Brother claimed on "The Ellen DeGeneres Show" at the timethat she was the one who hung up on him. Next up was Harry Styles, who reportedly received a passive aggressive shout-out during an MTV VMA acceptance speech. Then there was John Mayer, who told Rolling Stone he was "really humiliated" by Swift's song "Dear John" and "didn't deserve it." (Honestly, what do you expect when a grown man dates a teenager?) Calvin Harris may have seen Swift's ugliest side after their 2016 split. In some now-deleted tweets (via Stereogum), the DJ accused her of trying to tear him down "for something to do." Their relationship was also subject to cheating rumors, which Swift's "Reputation" lyrics didn't do a great job of dispelling. In addition, Cosmopolitan accused Swift of throwing actor Tom Hiddleston under the bus with "Getaway Car," which is to say nothing of the songs inspired by her splits from Jake Gyllenhaal and Joe Alwyn. Moral of the story is: If you don't want a Taylor Swift breakup song written about you, marry her. (We're looking at you, Travis Kelce.) Tristan Thompson repeatedly cheated on Khloé Kardashian Jerritt Clark/Getty Images Tristan Thompson and Khloé Kardashian began dating in 2016, just a couple of months before his ex-girlfriend, model Jordan Craig, gave birth to his first child, Prince. Unfortunately for Kardashian, her pregnancies with the NBA star would also be tainted by the presence of other women. In April 2018, multiple reports of infidelity surfaced. First, TMZ spotted Thompson going to a hotel room with a mystery woman when the reality star was nine months pregnant with daughter True. The outlet then obtained video of him kissing two other women at a hookah lounge when Kardashian was three months pregnant. And it didn't end there. While Kardashian initially chose to stay with Thompson, she eventually called it quits in February 2019 after learning her man had cheated on her with Kylie Jenner's BFF, Jordyn Woods.
